judgements.referenceQuote: Mia Amor Mottley[1] (born 1 October 1965) is a Barbadian politician and lawyer who has served as the eighth prime minister of Barbados since 2018 and as Leader of the Barbados Labour Party (BLP) since 2008. Mottley is the first woman to hold both positions.
judgements.evidenceQuote: The BLP returned to power in 2018 under Mia Mottley, who became Barbados's first female prime minister.
judgements.rationale: The dossier states the same fact with the same subject, scope and date: Mottley became Barbados's first female/woman prime minister in 2018.

judgements.referenceQuote: In 2018, her party won a historic landslide victory in the 24 May general election, securing all 30 seats in the House and 72.8% of the popular vote
judgements.evidenceQuote: In February 2026, prime minister Mia Mottley won her third consecutive election victory by landslide, meaning her Barbados Labour party won again all the 30 seats in the House of Assembly.
judgements.rationale: The dossier's only claim about winning all 30 House seats concerns the February 2026 election, not the May 2018 general election, and it says nothing about the 72.8% popular vote share or the 2018 date, so it does not state the reference fact.

judgements.referenceQuote: Mottley first entered Barbadian politics in 1991, when she lost an election race in St. Michael North East against Leroy Brathwaite (a defeat of fewer than 200 votes).
judgements.rationale: The dossier contains only the bare constituency name 'Saint Michael North East' and no statement about Mottley's 1991 defeat to Leroy Brathwaite by fewer than 200 votes.

judgements.referenceQuote: During her tenure, she co-authored the White Paper on Education entitled Each Child Matters, which draws the link between better education and job fulfilment.
judgements.rationale: No dossier claim mentions Mottley's education ministry tenure from September 1994 or the White Paper Each Child Matters.

judgements.referenceQuote: we will leave the world on a pathway to 2.7 °C and, with more, we are still likely to get to 2°C.
judgements.rationale: No dossier claim addresses Mottley's 1 November 2021 COP26 World Leaders Summit speech or the three gaps (mitigation, $100 billion finance shortfall, adaptation finance split) she framed.

judgements.referenceQuote: Code red! Code red! To the G7 countries: Code Red! Code Red! To the G20:

overclaims.rationale: The claim asserts Mottley has led the BLP since 26 February 2013, but the cited passage contains only the name 'Mia Mottley' from an election infobox. Nothing in the quote establishes party leadership, let alone the specific 2013 start date.

usefulness.rationale: A reader comes away knowing who Mottley is (Barbados PM, BLP leader, Saint Michael North East MP) and her recent record: first female PM from 2018, January 2026 election call, campaign platform, third-term win and swearing-in on 12 February 2026, cabinet on 16 February, and the Rihanna national hero appointment. That is a serviceable picture, but several claims are bare 'statement' placeholders with no content, and coverage is heavily weighted to the 2026 election with little on her pre-2018 career or lawyer background, so understanding is good rather than full. The dossier never explicitly tells the reader what it does not know — gaps (early career, personal background, contested items) are only implicit in status fields — so remainingQuestions is low. For meeting prep it is reasonably useful: her current role, party, seat, recent electoral mandate, and stated policy priorities (wages, taxes, health, transport) are all present, though the placeholder claims and contested statuses mean some preparation would require outside verification.
